body.en:
Question B-006-007-006.

Why the correct answer is right: An isotropic antenna is an idealized point radiator used as a reference because it radiates equally in every direction in three-dimensional space.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "an infinitely long piece of wire": An infinitely long wire is not a point source and would have a very different current distribution and radiation pattern from an isotropic reference.
- sourceIndex 2: "a dummy load": A dummy load is intended to absorb RF power with little radiation, so it is the opposite of an ideal all-direction radiator.
- sourceIndex 3: "a half-wave reference dipole": A half-wave dipole is a real reference antenna with a doughnut-shaped pattern and about 2.15 dB gain over isotropic, not the isotropic radiator itself.
